newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes firm on latex covering.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes firm on latex covering.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended firm after some latex short-covering for the Chinese market in early trading, dealers said.
But business was thin, with consumer demand staying weak despite a late rebound in Tokyo futures.
"The evening was quietly steady, with no signs of business except for the slight sales in the morning," said a dealer.

Traders reported sales of two hundred to three hundred tonnes of drum latex, which pushed up offer prices of the material to 240 Malaysian cents (95 cents) a kg, a sharp jump from Thursday's 235 cents.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board qouted December RSS1 buyer at 321 cents a kg, unchanged from Thursday. December SMR 20 was half cent higher at 310.50.
Trading houses quoted the SMR CV at 366, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 322, SMR 10 at 312 and SMR 20 at 310.
"My guess is the SMR 20 would be four to five cents higher next week while the RSS1 stays unchanged," said a dealer.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 245.09 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 7 from 244.84 on Nov 6. The daily indicator price rose to 245.60 from 245.17.
